Imagine Sector Mechanicus pillars... but shorter! That's pretty much it.

The main files provided have a notional height of 58.5mm, which means that they're the same height as Zone Mortalis pillars and walls. So this is nice if you want some cross-compatibility.
It also means that pillars + platform + pillars = the height of a regular full-height 122mm Sec Mech pillar. So you can muck about with shorter levels that still tie into the big ones.
They have pegs on top to locate into standard Sec Mech platforms. They are a slightly looser fit, intentionally, so be prepared to use glue rather than rely on push-fit.

"F" models are a full pair of pillars.
"L" and "R", you guessed it, are left and right pillars. I found it easier to support single pillars the way I wanted, and the split is barely noticeable when assembled.
If you print separate pillars, you can of course combine any L with any R.
All of them play nicely with mirroring, which does not affect the mating, so _theoretically_ there are 100 different combinations (since you wouldn't bother to mirror the ones with no greebles or the 0 greebles).

"reg_sup.zip" contains all separate pillars, supported exactly as I printed them for myself.

If you want a slightly taller pillar, with a notional height of 61mm (i.e. half a regular pillar by itself), then look in the "tall.zip" folder. It's the same details, just adapted for a pillars with a taller lintel to make this possible.
These might be useful to you if you're already using 61mm terrain pieces, e.g. [SevenUnited's Half Furnace 2](https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:6503327).
I don't want this height and therefore have not printed them, so you'll have to support them yourself.

Justification du tag SUP :

“reg_sup.zip” contains all separate pillars, supported exactly as I printed them for myself.

So you want a large Sector Mechanicus tile, and you don't want greebly detail? And, maybe, you have a fairly small resin printer, so printing it in one piece isn't really possible? OK, or maybe you have a big enough printer?

Here's a few options for 122mm octagonal or square tiles. They match the dimensions you would expect for Sector Mechanicus. They have all the join-y holes underneath.

Unlike [my other large tile offering](https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:6962622) these have no locators on top. The bolts are recessed and do not protrude at all (not even like regular SM tiles), so you can stack whatever you like on top.

Your choice whether you want a port in the middle (and what orientation) or not.

If you are printing tiny little parts on your tiny little printer, then you will want:
* 1x centre piece, whether that's a square or a port
* 4x outer section, suited to port or not as appropriate
 Technically you can mix the oct (non diag) and square sections, I guess, if you want an unusual shape
 (e.g. if you were making [a big platform](https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:7092618), say)

If you don't care about splitting up your tile, then just print one of the full ones, or a quarter/half. These are designed to stand alone as regular tiles. If you can fit it on your printer, it'll be easier than assembling 5 parts to make a single tile!

There's a zip file named "fdm" containing all the whole-tile pieces with no recesses (except the join-y holes) underneath. I have _not_ tested them on an FDM printer; I do not own one. It just seemed maybe useful.

This looks _suspiciously_ like my [Modular Utility Building](https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:6838588), don't you think? 
OK, yeah, I fancied having one that was full height - that is, the same height as a GW Sector Fronteris hab block, and therefore also the same height as a [Fronteris style bunker](https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:6988922). It is, very approximately, 60x60x70mm.
For my own use I thought I'd go all in on the vents; make it some sort of cooling tower type thing, with a simple style vaguely influenced by some belfry louvres. I've kept in some more basic walls too, if that's more your style (or you plan to embellish them yourself).

### Compatibility

Style-wise, it obviously takes heavy cues from the Sector Fronteris hab units.

The pipe ports are the standard size expected on GW's 40k terrain - 25.6mm diameter.

The side pipe ports have a centre-line height of 14.5mm, which matches other terrain, e.g. Thermic Plasma Conduits.. Their outer face is 30.5mm from the centre point, so if you have two opposite each other they'll be 61mm apart, which should be a familiar size to those used to e.g. Sector Mechanicus components.

The roof is the same height as that of a Sector Fronteris hab unit, and the roof with a port should match the ports on those hab units too.

### Assembly

You will need:
* 4x *pillars*
* 4x *walls*
* 1x *roof*
If you chose walls with *ports*, you'll also need
* 1+ *pipe ends*

Walls push into pillars from behind. I recommend putting the roof in unglued as you put together the rest, then gluing it in last.

Pillars can be mirrored for a bit more variety.

### Pre-supports

The supported files here are the way I did them for myself, successfully. Is it the best? No. The walls and pillars are definitely over-supported, but I wasn't going to go back and change something that worked.

As you may see from the pictures, I did _not_ print non-louvred walls. The supports have been applied in the same way, but I have not actually printed these specifically.

### FAQ

* What's with the extra holes on the pipe ports in the photos but not on the STLs?
 _I have bizarre hopes of putting a lot of magnets everywhere. I'm not doing this in a way that I think makes sense to most people, so I didn't think it was worth sharing those. You can have the clean ones that actually look good by themselves!_

Justification du tag SUP :

The supported files here are the way I did them for myself, successfully. Is it the best? No. The walls and pillars are definitely over-supported, but I wasn’t going to go back and change something that worked.

Sector Mechanicus style tiles.
Simpler - no details in the gratings. Sometimes you don't need all the detail. 
Many of them have pipe ports, which oddly don't exist in the originals outside a ruined one. 

Standard holes underneath for pillars and join-y connector-y things.

I needed a single rectangular tile with a port for myself. But, you know, with what I needed to make for that one, I could make multiple permutations. I'd done half the work already (It might seem like I'd done more than half, but making the permutations took way longer than I expected!).

1x1 square tiles, and 1x2 tiles, and a single strange 1x1.5 tile.
Two different gratings (plain and with a cog design), plus pipe ports in different positions and numbers, with hatches at various orientations.
Honestly, yeah, it's overkill. I do not know how many people care about getting hatches in the every possible orientation, but well, the person sitting in my chair really is that ridiculous.

The *FDM* zip file contains the exact same tiles, but without the recesses underneath. They still have holes for pegs; there's no other changes. I _have not_ printed these in FDM. I don't even have an FDM printer. It was a suggestion someone made to me, seeing as the simpler nature of the top detail might lend itself to FDM printing, and I figured, sure, why not. May as well, right? Perhaps this is useful to someone, perhaps not.

* What's with the 2-port tiles' letter-number designations? Why are some numbers missing?
 A/O/S = Aligned/Opposite/Symmetric. The numbers are missing because some would be equivalent (e.g. O1 == S1, A3 == S3), or creatable simply by rotating/mirroring an existing piece (e.g. A4 would be A2 mirrored)

So you have some Thermic Plasma Conduits™ (or locally sourced alternative with the same dimensions), but rather than having them pretty much on the ground, you want them a bit higher to make things interesting. Say, with a centre-line height of 61mm off the table, which is exactly the right height to match up with the mid-line of several Sector Mechanicus™ components, how about that?

Well, have I got good news for you: I had this exact requirement and made myself a pillar type thingy that has a good deal of visual congruity with Sector Mechanicus™ pillars.

Honestly, there's not much more to say. The pipe foot bit itself is very simple and is not imitating the originals, but it does the same job and has very similar tolerances - it's just snug enough that I can pick up the pipe and the pillars come with, but aren't jammed in.

I have also included a basic pipe foot without the pillar, in case you have other stuff on the ground and want it to match. Lots of people have made pipe feet that do this job though, so take it or leave it!

The supported files (ending in "_sup") are what I printed with and was happy with. YMMV. I am definitely not an expert.
